title: Rooms — Watch — payload
description: A member asks a room's host to send a content-free `rooms/changed` signal to an address the member names when the room moves past a version the member has read to. A one-shot watch sends one signal per arming, and the member re-arms after it has caught up; a live watch (`live: true`), permitted only on a room whose signal delay is `none`, sends one each time the room moves past the version last signalled, coalesced to at most one a second, for a lease of at most 120 seconds the member renews while the room is on screen. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

roomId.description: The room to watch. A host verifies the presentation against credentials issued by this identifier, never against a member list of its own.

presentation.description: Must confer `read` at this room's scope — the grant a listing takes, since a signal says no more than a listing would.

address.description: The DID the host sends the signal to, over a transport that DID's document advertises and the host speaks. Chosen by the member. It identifies the watch: a request naming the same room and address re-arms or cancels that watch, and one naming another address is another watch. On a `private` room it MUST be a DID the member uses for nothing else (*Security & Privacy*).

sinceVersion.description: The highest version of the room the member has read to — the watermark it would pass as `sinceVersion` to `rooms/records/list`. The host signals as soon as the room's latest version is above it, at once if it already is, so that a change landing between the member's last listing and this request is not missed. Absent means the room's latest version when the host arms the watch, which a member that has just listed the room may rely on only if it accepts missing a change made in between.

leaseSeconds.description: How long the member asks the watch to last if it does not fire, in seconds, up to 30 days. A host MAY grant less, and says what it granted in `expiresAt`; for a live watch it grants at most 120 seconds whatever is asked. Absent means the host's default.

live.description: Arm, or renew, a live watch: a signal each time the room moves past the version last signalled, coalesced to at most one a second, for a lease of at most 120 seconds. Only `true` is meaningful, so only `true` is accepted; a one-shot watch omits the member. Permitted only on a room whose signal delay is `none` — refused otherwise with `rooms/watch:liveNotPermitted`. A member renews a live watch by sending the same room and address with `live: true` before `expiresAt`, and asks for one only while the room is on its person's screen. A host ignores it on a cancel.

cancel.description: End the watch on this room and address, one-shot or live. Only `true` is meaningful, so only `true` is accepted. A producer sends neither `sinceVersion`, `leaseSeconds` nor `live` with it, and a host ignores them on a cancel. A cancel of a watch the host does not hold succeeds and says `armed: false`, so a retry is harmless.

armed.description: `true`: the watch is armed — a one-shot watch will send one signal to `address` the first time the room is above `sinceVersion`, or has sent it already because the room was; a live watch (`live`) sends one each time the room moves past the version last signalled until `expiresAt`. `false`: the watch was cancelled, or there was none to cancel.

live.description: Present when the watch armed is live. Absent when it is one-shot — including when a live watch was asked of a host that implements only 0.1, which arms a one-shot watch: a member treats a watch as live only when this says so.

expiresAt.description: Present when `armed` is `true`: when the host forgets the watch if it has not fired, or, for a live watch, when it ends unless renewed — the lease granted, at most 120 seconds from the request for a live watch, never later than the earliest instant at which any credential of the presentation stops being valid.
